newsitem.title: DUBAI: Banks lead Saudi stocks up three pct in busy week.
newsitem.headline: Banks lead Saudi stocks up three pct in busy week.

text.p: Bullish sentiment on banks helped lift Saudi Arabian stocks almost three percent higher in more active trade last week, figures from the Riyadh-based Bakheet Financial Advisors (BFA) showed on Sunday.
The index moved up 2.99 percent to close at 153.91 points on Thursday from the previous week's 149.44 points. Of the 58 companies traded, 25 rose, 20 slipped and 13 were unchanged.

Banks accounted for 41 percent of trading volume, which BFA said rose to nearly 4.83 million shares worth almost 1.17 billion riyals ($312 million) from the previous week's 3.35 million shares worth 634.97 million riyals.
Leading the gainers were Arab National Bank, which was up 13.6 percent at 561 riyals and Saudi American Bank, which rose 13.4 percent to 618 riyals.
Saudi British Bank was over nine percent firmer at 589 riyals and Saudi Hollandi Bank was another winner, closing four percent higher at 435. Al-Bank al-Saudi al-Fransi was up nine riyals at 252.
The most active share in the week was Riyad Bank, which accounted for some 19 percent of volume and value traded. It closed two riyals firmer at 239 riyals, BFA figures show.
Outside the banking sector, services stocks accounted for 22 percent and cement stocks made up 21 percent of turnover.
Southern Cement was 4.1 percent better at 430 riyals.
Among the week's losers were al-Mawashi al-Mukairish 50 percent, down seven percent at 39 riyals and National Industrialisation Co, which was four riyals weaker at 65 riyals.
